label: HOLD LENGTH, THE WHOLE RANGE
v: Sources disagree on how long the core must stay above 93 C (200 F). Cap n Stem: 1-3 h as a general standard, about 2 h in a container with a strong boiler, 3 h called overkill. The textbook working rule: at least 2-3 h, at most 4-6 h, proved by a logger. Avery: 4-5 h. Joseph's own log sheet: 4-6 h above 200 F. Joseph confirmed 4 h for this farm, so the log judges against 4 h and shows the others here as context.
source: SOURCES DISAGREE. CAP N STEM IS FINAL WHERE THEY DO, BUT JOSEPH SET 4 H.

label: WHEN THE SHORT END IS SAFE
v: The shorter holds rely on a fast-steaming boiler and a measured cold spot. Log your own runs and compare yield and contamination before shortening the hold.

label: THE SLOWEST BLOCK DECIDES
v: The probe in the slowest-heating block decides the run, not the box air. On a barrel with an element at the bottom, the bottom blocks cook 4-5 h longer than the top ones that the run is timed on.

label: TOTAL TIME IS NOT HOLD TIME
v: A run described as 10 hours total can be a 3 hour hold at the core. Always say which one you mean. This log keeps come-up, hold above each temperature, and total separately.

label: WHY OVERPROCESSING MATTERS
v: Time and temperature trade off. Overcooked blocks are chemically altered, roasted or caramelized, and colonize poorly. Anything above 96 C (205 F) counts as overprocessing on the sheet, and the sheet wants under 3 h there.

label: WHAT THE F VALUE IS
v: F adds up the killing effect of the whole curve as hours at 97 C. For each interval, F = hours x 10^((T - 97) / z), summed. The sheet does not give z. 10 C is a common working value for bacterial spores, so an hour at 87 C counts as 0.1 h and an hour at 107 C as 10 h.
source: TEXTBOOK T12 (AN EXPLANATION ADDED THERE, NOT ON THE SHEET)

label: DOOR OPENINGS SHOW ON THE LOGGER
v: Opening the doors acts as a purge. On a small steam box, adding a forgotten rack made the temperature climb 17-22 C faster than before. Note door openings in the run notes.

label: STERILIZING AT PRESSURE
v: Sterilization needs 15 psi (1 bar) and 121 C (250 F). The textbook minimum for grain and water jars is about 35 min. Avery holds 1 h 45 min at 17 psi on the stopcock 75X. Never leave a stovetop canner unattended while heating.
